section1.bio: I've been coding back-end for years using Laravel, Node.js, Python, .NET, and Java — but the stack is just a tool. What matters is solving real problems. summary.title: Professional summary
summary.paragraph1: My main focus is backend engineering and building institutional systems. I work with Laravel/PHP, Node.js/TypeScript, and Java/Spring Boot, using PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and other technologies depending on each solution's requirements.
summary.paragraph2: I build REST APIs, system integrations, authentication, access control, auditing, queues, and asynchronous processing. I also work on frontend applications with Vue.js and React when a project calls for full-stack work.
summary.paragraph2b: I also have hands-on experience hosting and publishing sites on AWS (including automated deploys with GitHub Actions to Amazon S3 and CloudFront), Docker, remote server access and management via SSH, file transfer over FTP/SFTP, and WordPress.
summary.paragraph3: My experience includes academic systems, research platforms, editorial solutions, automations, and institutional applications built for UniEVANGÉLICA, Fábrica de Tecnologias Turing, and the Brazilian Air Force. I have a growing interest in software architecture, cloud, observability, security, and applied AI for business systems.

aila.title: Aila — Smart Peer Reviewer Recommendation
aila.problem: Finding qualified reviewers who match a manuscript's topic is slow, manual work for a journal's editorial team.
aila.impact: Supports the selection of scientific peer reviewers through ranking, editorial history, and recurrence analysis, reducing reliance on manual searches during the review process.
aila.roleShort: I built the whole system on my own: a Python/FastAPI backend with local-AI classification, reviewer ranking and invitation history, plus the Nuxt/Vue frontend.
aila.result: Structured ranking of reviewers matched to manuscripts, with recurrence and invitation history.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: A platform supporting the scientific editorial process, using academic data and review history to help identify reviewers who match a given manuscript.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: The system handles thematic classification of manuscripts via local AI, reviewer ranking, invitation history, reviewer recurrence, and editorial rules — cutting reliance on manual searches and improving traceability of the selection process.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: Python/FastAPI backend on PostgreSQL, with local AI via Ollama (plus a cloud fallback) for thematic classification, semantic embeddings for reviewer ranking, and a Nuxt/Vue frontend. Authentication with Argon2, RBAC, and in-house auditing.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Full ownership of the system (backend, frontend, and tests): modeling the reviewer domain, ranking, invitation history, local-AI integration, and editorial rules.

tabs.title: Results
content: Structured ranking of reviewers matched to manuscripts, cutting manual searches in a scientific journal's editorial process.

esports.title: E-Sports UniEVANGÉLICA Portal — 5th edition
esports.problem: A recurring institutional e-sports tournament needed per-modality registration and a public history of past editions.
esports.impact: Tournament registration and management system with versioned editions, allowing the 4th edition to be archived and the 5th launched without losing public history.
esports.roleShort: Lead author of both backend and frontend, including the versioned-edition system and the backend's security layer.
esports.result: 5th edition published with a versioned-edition system, preserving the 4th edition's history.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: An institutional e-sports tournament with multiple editions over time, requiring per-modality registration, edition-specific rules, and a public history of past editions.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: A versioned-edition model (theme, schedule, and rules isolated per edition) that let the 5th edition take over the home page while keeping the 4th accessible as history, with per-modality registration and an admin area.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: NestJS backend with Sequelize/PostgreSQL, httpOnly cookie session auth, honeypot, and per-route rate limiting. Frontend in Nuxt with Tailwind CSS.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Lead author on both backend and frontend: modeling the edition system, per-modality registration, versioned rules, and the security layer (session, honeypot, rate limiting, auditing).

tabs.title: Results
content: 5th edition published with a versioned-edition system, preserving the 4th edition's history.

jac.title: JAC – Academic and Community Journey
jac.problem: Tracking attendance at academic events by hand is slow and easy to fake, with no real visibility into who actually showed up.
jac.impact: Academic event management system with QR-code and geolocation check-in, and gamified point rewards. An advanced personal project, with 100+ automated tests.
jac.roleShort: I built the entire architecture (backend and frontend), the geospatial and QR-code check-in, and drove documented remediation of security vulnerabilities.
jac.result: Backend and frontend with automated tests and deploy pipelines configured across multiple platforms.

tabs.title: Context

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: QR-code and geolocation (geofencing) check-in, a points and rewards system, and an admin panel with dashboards, built with engineering discipline (tests, documented vulnerability remediation).

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: Node.js/Express backend with Prisma and PostgreSQL, strict TypeScript validated across three distinct build targets (Node, Cloudflare Workers, production). React/Vite/Tailwind frontend with Vitest and Playwright.

tabs.title: My role

lionFanstone.title: Lion — James Fanstone System Rewrite
lionFanstone.problem: An institutional academic-research system built in Laravel needed to move to a more sustainable foundation without interrupting the system already in production.
lionFanstone.impact: Backend rewrite of an institutional academic-research platform, migrating from a legacy production system to a new Java/Spring Boot architecture.
lionFanstone.roleShort: I'm solely leading the backend's architectural rewrite, with real CNPq/Lattes integration. Still in development, not yet published to production.
lionFanstone.result: Rewrite in progress with full ownership, CI configured, and automated tests.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: UniEVANGÉLICA's institutional academic-research system (where I contributed specific features, like enrollment and notice reports, on the legacy Laravel system) needed to move to a more sustainable foundation, migrating the research domain to a new architecture.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: Incremental backend rewrite in Java/Spring Boot covering researchers, academic output, Qualis/CAPES classification, projects, groups, notices, work plans, and external peer review via secure token, with resume import through real CNPq/Lattes (SOAP) integration.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: Java 21, Spring Boot 4, PostgreSQL with Flyway (versioned migrations, no automatic schema changes), Spring Security via session/cookie, ArchUnit for architecture rules, CI via GitHub Actions.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Full ownership of the rewrite: architecture, domain modeling, migrations, SOAP integration with CNPq/Lattes, and decisions documented via ADRs. Work still in development (an intermediate phase of a module-by-module migration plan), not yet published to production.

tabs.title: Results
content: Rewrite in progress, with CI configured and automated tests (JUnit, Mockito, ArchUnit) covering the domain already migrated.
